authority: Explicit user instruction: complete official GNUnet protocol interoperability with Rust-native internals and better layering, architecture and performance.

reference_target.update_rule: Recheck official releases and standards; review protocol differences and refresh affected evidence before changing the pinned interoperability target. Do not mix incompatible versions silently.

external_contract: Official message identifiers, serialized fields, widths, byte order, canonical encodings and public protocol artifacts.
Cryptographic algorithms, key/identity encodings, signature inputs, KDF domains, authentication, key updates and replay rejection.
Required network and public service IPC operations, responses, framing, flow control and protocol-defined ordering.
Protocol-visible error, cancellation, reconnect, restart and recovery behavior; distinguish transmission, remote processing and durability.
Every required external capability has versioned implementation status and real unchanged-official-C interoperability evidence.
internal_design_freedom: Rust API names, type shapes, ownership, allocation and resource storage.
Scheduling, async runtime, queues, task topology, concurrency and buffering.
Static enum/trait registries or Rust extension mechanisms instead of the C plugin ABI and dynamic loader.
Single-process or separate-process service composition, with required public protocols preserved.
Internal database schema and persistence mechanisms, except externally standardized artifacts and explicitly supported interchange formats.
Logging and helper implementation details, except explicitly promised external configuration or command interfaces.
rust_quality_contract: Protocol and service cores have no OS/runtime/database or facade dependency.
Shared generic runtime has no dependency on a specific service client such as STATISTICS.
State, identities, cancellation and cleanup have explicit owners; no stale completion can affect another instance.
Queues and expensive work have explicit resource bounds/backpressure; native unsafe boundaries remain small and auditable.
Traits and crate boundaries represent actual variation or ownership boundaries rather than one wrapper per C function.
Preserve useful no_std profiles without forcing host services into unnecessary embedded-style APIs.
Performance claims require repeatable comparable workloads, identical protocol/security behavior, and measured latency, throughput, CPU, memory and allocations.

reference_inventory_policy.external_inventory_origin: Complete official protocol messages, service capabilities, externally visible operations and state contracts; source inventories are supporting discovery material, not the definition of required Rust APIs.

evidence_policy.external_interop: Real C-to-Rust, Rust-to-C and mixed-node end-to-end execution, with current source/target/profile/artifact identities and negative/recovery cases.
evidence_policy.rust_quality: Architecture checks, meaningful Rust correctness/resource tests and measured benchmarks; quality evidence cannot impersonate official-C interoperability.
evidence_policy.historical_reports: Keep original source/profile/scope; a policy change does not relabel old reports or award verified status.

gate_transition.legacy_gate: Canonical check-conformance now checks external release requirements in both modes. check-legacy-conformance and check-api-inventory retain historical C catalog audits without product release authority.
required_next_steps: Build the complete external operation/message/profile matrix independently of C helper signatures.

Independently review complete semantic inventories and real profile/direction slots. Stage2 expresses the FS38/147/18 draft without resolving734 original review obligations or granting implementation/release readiness.
Migrate all required producers and reviewed semantic evidence adapters with current source/build/profile bindings and meaningful omission/false-credit controls.
Rerun affected real interoperability evidence on the resulting implementation.
